items.title: WW2 Expert Answers Hitler Questions
items.description:
Did Hitler fight in WW1? What happened in the bunker? Did Hitler have a micro penis? 

Join historian Emma Craigie as she answers your questions about Adolf Hitler.

Emma Craigie is the author of four books including the critically acclaimed novel 'Chocolate Cake with Hitler', and co-author of the Sunday Times best-seller 'Hitler's Last Day: Minute by Minute'

00:00 Intro Highlights
00:31 Introduction by Author Emma Craigie
01:01 Was Hitler German or Austrian?
01:24 Did Hitler have a bad childho
items.why_watch: Historian Emma Craigie, co-author of 'Hitler's Last Day: Minute by Minute,' cuts through decades of myth and tabloid distortion to answer reader questions with actual archival grounding. The Q&A format means she tackles both serious historical questions (his WWI service, the bunker's final hours) and the more absurd ones with equal precision. If you've ever wanted a trustworthy corrective to the noise around this subject, this is a compact 31 minutes with a genuinely knowledgeable guide.

discovery_articles.title: Durham Town Hall in Durham, England
discovery_articles.snippet: The Town Hall has been central to Durham's history since 1350 and has opened its doors to the public following refurbishment work. Now everyone can discover its rich history and hidden stories. Audio guides, interactive information points and short films help you to explore this extraordinary building and the remarkable individuals who helped shape the city.

discovery_articles.title: Liverpool’s First Enclosed Dock in Liverpool, England
discovery_articles.snippet: In a subterranean chamber under the massive Liverpool ONE shopping centre is the infrastructure that turned Liverpool from a lacklustre port city into a global powerhouse of shipping. While the city got it's charter back in 1207 with the intention of it being a port city, it struggled to gain much success. It was overshadowed by nearby Chester and lacked decent infrastructure; Loading and unloading ships was very slow, sometimes taking weeks to unload, as ships would anchor in the deep water of the estuary while small boats would shuttle cargo between them and the city.

news.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for brown butter apple and blackberry bars | The sweet spot
news.snippet: A bar for the bountiful season, with a rubbly oat crust, a soft fruit filling and a crisp topping September is always a wistful time for me. Summer has all but slipped away, the days are noticeably shorter and the children are heading back to school. But there is comfort, too, in settling back into familiar routines.
news.blurb: A timely reminder that September's soft melancholy is best met with brown butter, hedgerow fruit, and something oat-topped cooling on the rack.

recipe.title: High Summer Lunch Salad
recipe.snippet: This substantial lunch salad brings together peak summer tomatoes and pluots with protein-rich mung beans and a simple vinaigrette. Fried shallots and pistachios bring the crunch, while rings of banana pepper add a bit of kick and a pop of color! Continue reading High Summer Lunch Salad on 101 Cookbooks
recipe.blurb: A proper high-summer lunch that lets peak-season tomatoes and pluots shine alongside mung beans, pistachios, and fried shallots — substantial enough to feel celebratory, simple enough to actually make.

larder.seasonal_note: Zürich's Saturday markets at Bürkliplatz are piling high with Zwetschgen right now — those deep-violet Swiss plums that beg to be halved and laid over a buttery Zwetschgenwähe, their tartness mellowing into something almost jammy in a hot oven on a cool morning.
